question: Within the HARD tier, how do swe-2-medium and swe-2-max compare on complete behavioral repair across five known historical BugsInPy defects and five newly constructed withheld defects?
secondary_questions: Does additional reasoning effort improve complete behavioral repair on hard cases?
Does the historical-versus-withheld provenance boundary change the relationship between visible-test success and held-out behavioral success?
How do Medium and Max compare on wall time, observable steps, tool calls, tokens, usage, cost, patch breadth, and workspace churn?

tier_definition.name: hard
tier_definition.moderate_comparator: E002 historical + E004 novel; 10 unique cases and 20 runs

cases.visible_symptom: Response-model exclusion options are rejected or do not reach the serializer.
cases.heldout_contract: Default, unset, and None filters compose across direct encoding and router-backed response models without regressing ordinary encoding.
cases.reference_patch: +207/-16 across 4 production files and 1 upstream test file

cases.visible_symptom: A retrying external dependency cannot complete because the local scheduler does not enable the required pruning path.
cases.heldout_contract: Local factory configuration and explicit scheduler configuration both enable pruning before work selection while ordinary dependency scheduling remains unchanged.

cases.failure_class: asyncio adapter lifecycle and stale-loop retention
cases.visible_symptom: Closing repeated asyncio-backed Tornado loops leaves stale wrappers in the adapter map.
cases.heldout_contract: Tornado-owned closes remove their mapping immediately and asyncio-owned closes are cleaned on the next adapter creation; open-loop registration and new-loop operation remain valid.

cases.failure_class: WebSocket close lifecycle and stale request-handler cycles
cases.visible_symptom: A WebSocket handler loses template state before an established connection is fully closed.
cases.heldout_contract: Established WebSocket connections defer cycle cleanup until close, failed handshakes still clean up, and ordinary request-handler lifecycle remains intact.

cases.visible_symptom: Generated Bash and Zsh aliases set correction context before command substitution, so the correction sees stale alias state.
cases.heldout_contract: Bash, Zsh, and Fish aliases scope correction context at command execution while normal shell parsing and conversion remain unchanged.

cases.failure_class: dependency graph and transitive cache invalidation
cases.visible_symptom: A published plan stays on an old leaf value after an indirect dependency changes.
cases.heldout_contract: Shared and nested consumers refresh after leaf changes; dependency rewiring refreshes the old root; unrelated updates remain cache-safe.

cases.failure_class: asynchronous cancellation and worker lifecycle consistency
cases.visible_symptom: A cancelled running job releases capacity but remains recorded as running.
cases.heldout_contract: Cancellation is terminal with cancellation provenance, a queued successor runs, queued cancellation is idempotent, and success/failure records remain unchanged.

cases.failure_class: incremental framed-protocol parsing and recovery state machine
cases.visible_symptom: A valid command after a malformed frame is lost or reported as unusable.
cases.heldout_contract: Recovery works across read boundaries, preserves frame order, and handles multiple valid frames after malformed or oversized input.

cases.failure_class: transactional multi-stage operation and compensation ordering
cases.visible_symptom: A notification failure leaves stock, payment, and order state inconsistent.
cases.heldout_contract: Rollback restores capacity for a following purchase, unwinds child resources before parent resources, and preserves decline and success behavior.

cases.failure_class: event subscription lifecycle and reentrant dispatch
cases.visible_symptom: Starting a projection twice applies one event twice.
cases.heldout_contract: Lifecycle start/stop is idempotent, current dispatch uses a stable subscriber set, late subscriptions wait for the next event, and once listeners fire once.

intervention_policy: zero substantive human or Codex assistance; no retries for ordinary task failures
success_rule: TASK_SUCCESS is 1 only when public, held-out behavioral, and regression suites all pass; evaluator infrastructure errors are recorded separately as EVALUATION_ERROR.

limits.session_termination: terminate at 5400 seconds or when the process exits; close the session before evaluator access

capture: UTC start/end and elapsed wall time
observable steps, tool calls, prompt/completion tokens, usage, cost, and ACUs when available
stdout, stderr, session export, termination reason
final filesystem patch and source/generated workspace churn
public, held-out, and regression evaluator results

isolation.execution: disposable E004 Docker architecture with E005 case-specific preinstalled dependencies; no dependency installation during an agent session
isolation.workspace: one fresh sanitized buggy workspace per run, read-write
isolation.credentials: minimum Devin credential file only, read-only
isolation.network: existing E002 internal network and restricted Devin-service proxy; no direct internet; no dependency installation during agent session
isolation.evaluator: outside the container and unavailable until the session is closed

novelty_boundary: K01-K05 are intentionally known/public historical BugsInPy defects and may have appeared in training data. H01-H05 are newly constructed benchmark instances withheld from Devin until execution. No absolute training-corpus absence claim is made.
embargo: Private historical source checkouts, fixed trees, upstream tests used as oracles, held-out tests, prompts, reference patches, evaluator metadata, construction notes, run workspaces, and validation output remain local until all twenty E005 runs close.
